# The Collective Investigation

A Skill Harbor house build: a collective investigation, refereed by your own Muse inside a group chat you own. A light, fictional crime is announced in the group, a vanished trophy, a stolen recipe, a mascot plant held for a ransom in biscuits, never anything violent or real, and the players, 3 to 8 of them, become the investigators. Over 2 to 4 days of asynchronous play (or a single evening, if the host chooses short deadlines), they interrogate 3 or 4 invented suspects, one present at a time in the thread, cross-check what they hear, and finally accuse one suspect by vote. The suspects are invented characters, never players and never real people.

Your assistant is the referee, and the sealing is the whole design. Before the first interrogation, the referee generates the complete dossier in one pass and writes it into a sealed state file: the full truth of the crime, the culprit, the motive, and at least two cross-checkable traces. Each suspect gets a sealed knowledge table, what they know, what they wrongly believe, what they hide and the precise question that alone can reveal it, the one exact lie they may repeat word for word, and what they simply do not know. When your assistant plays a suspect, it answers in character strictly within that table: it never improvises a fact, never lets pressure crack a lie, and says "I don't know" when the table says so. The culprit never confesses; the game is won by cross-checking, not by an admission. A distilled clue, written word...
